reason: The mucus layer fits over the ciliated lining to form the airway's first defensive surface.
expectation: The mucus and lining should form a surface that can trap inhaled material.

effect: The mucus-covered lining is ready to encounter inhaled particles; cilia can then move the mucus.
reaction: The trapping and clearance roles are clearly connected.
reason: The inhaled particles and bacteria should be caught by the mucus-covered lining.
expectation: The mucus should trap some of the inhaled material.

effect: The mucus trapped some inhaled material, but a few particles and bacteria reached deeper toward the air sacs.
reaction: The distinction between trapped and escaping material is useful.
reason: The beating cilia should move the particle-bearing mucus toward the throat.
expectation: Ciliary movement should carry trapped material toward the throat.

effect: The cilia now move trapped material toward the throat; material that reached the air sacs still needs attention.
reason: Lung macrophages are shown engulfing bacteria that reach the air sacs.
expectation: The macrophages should add a defense against some material that escaped the mucus.

effect: The attempted pairing instead connected the airway lining to the body; microbes still reach an air sac, where macrophages may act.
reaction: I was surprised the lining had to join the body before adding macrophages.
reason: Lung macrophages are positioned to engulf bacteria that reach the air sacs.

choice.combine: Body moving airway mucus toward the throat

expectation: Macrophages should deal with some microbes that escaped the airway mucus.

effect: The macrophages completed the airway defense model, showing a second defense against microbes that reach the air sacs, while acknowledging that defenses are imperfect.
reaction: The two complementary defenses make a satisfying conclusion.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following trapped particles from mucus to coordinated ciliary clearance made the protective mechanism concrete; the macrophage cutaway then showed what happens deeper in the lungs.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the moving airway lining to the body was a required intermediate step, but its purpose was less clear than the biological constructions around it.

surprise.text: I expected to add macrophages directly to the moving lining, but compatibility feedback instead connected the lining to the body first.

arbitrary.text: That required ordering felt somewhat arbitrary: the attempted pairing had a clear defensive rationale, although the automatic connection kept progress moving.

continue.text: I would continue: tracing how complementary structures protect the same body was interesting, even if the combinations were mostly predictable. The planned cutaways were clear, though how macrophages recognize microbes was only briefly stated.
